Framed is a pretty cool game. Gameplay is divided between multiple screens. On these screens, there are panels like a comic book. The aim is to re-arrange these panels to make the events of the comic play out differently, and the goal is usually to re-arrange the comic panels so that your character successfully outruns the police. Each screen should take a minute or a few to complete.

The gameplay isn't extremely original, but the presentation is everything here. Slick vector graphics using a 1960's aesthetic and silky smooth animations make this game drop-dead gorgeous. It's one of the best looking games you can get on a cell phone. Accompanying the excellent visuals is an equally excellent jazz soundtrack. As the pace slows down, the music becomes more reserved and elicits a feeling of suspense and the thrill of sneaking overtakes you. Suddenly, you're a grand strategist who just outplayed everyone. When the action ramps up, the music becomes more energetic and fills you with adrenaline. Suddenly, you're a quick-witted criminal who is one step ahead of everyone.

Framed isn't all roses and daisies, however. Every single screen amounts to essentially the same thing: Re-arrange tiles until your character successfully runs away. This seems obvious, but 80 screens in, the process can get tiring. There is also a limited amount of scenes as well, so Framed may get repetitive quickly. Relatively soon after starting, a new gameplay element is introduced wherein you can rotate a tile, but not re-arrange it in any other way. Rotating tiles is finicky and not very intuitive. There's also the issue of figuring out what certain tiles do. There may be 3 tiles on a screen that all look the same, but two may have debris fall as your character runs by. This makes certain screens exercises in trial and error, but this happens too rarely to hamper the experience too badly.

These small annoyances, however, are outweighed by the excellent soundtrack, gorgeous visuals, and fun gameplay. It's definitely worth the $4 entry fee to experience this game. If I had to give it a numerical score, an 8 would be appropriate. If you have a good pair of headphones that isolate sound, this is a great game to play on public transport because the levels are so short. Framed may have trouble keeping the player engaged in longer game sessions because of its simplicity.

Highly recommended
